steps.title: Dry Sémillon
steps.body: Young Hunter Sémillon suits oysters, sashimi and light seafood. Aged Hunter and dry Bordeaux blends suit roast chicken, crab, lobster, and creamy fish dishes. Margaret River Sémillon Sauvignon suits salads, goat's cheese and summer food.

steps.title: Sauternes
steps.body: Sauternes suits foie gras, a Bordeaux classic, and blue cheese, especially Roquefort, whose salt balances the sweetness. It also suits fruit tarts, crème brûlée and spicy Asian dishes. Serve at 8 to 10 degrees. Avoid desserts much sweeter than the wine.

steps.prompt: Match each Sémillon to a pairing.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve dry Sémillon at 8 to 11 degrees. Young Hunter is crisp and lean; wait 10 years for its magic. Dry white Bordeaux ages 10 to 20 years. Sauternes ages 20 to 50 years or more.

steps.prompt: Roquefort and Sauternes is a classic pairing.
steps.explanation: Yes. Salt balances sugar, and the wine's acidity cuts the cheese's fat.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Young dry Sémillon suits seafood; aged suits chicken and crab
Sauternes suits foie gras and Roquefort
Sémillon rewards ageing, dry or sweet
